Pregnancy is so spiritual! Midwives have believed so for a long, long time. I recently read and loved "Beyond Ourselves" by Catherine Marshall, she is such an old-school lady in the best way and her writing is so full of enthusiasm for the faith that it's contagious. She spends a chapter talking about one lady's testimony, a major part of which was a high-risk pregnancy preceeded by multiple losses. Her doctor actually told her, having no other explanation for her about her womb troubles, that a correlation had been found between pregnancy loss and feelings of guilt. Guilt during the pregnancy, not after. So the woman did all in her power, relying heavily on her church for support, to ground herself in her forgiven identity in Christ. Although she struggled with so much shame from her past, she was able to conquer it and her pregnancy was a healthy one. A beautiful real-life example and testimony from an excellent book. God bless you.

I had a termination when I was 18 due to health reasons. It crushed me. I’ve never felt so empty and broken. And I’ve held onto that feeling ever since. Years later, I had my son, and then my daughter. I’ve never mentioned this to them. One day, I was walking my son to school (he was 5 and we had gone to church together maybe twice), and he asked me if I remembered when he was in my tummy before? I was confused and asked if he meant when he was a baby? Because that I’ll never forget. But he said “No, the time before. You and Daddy decided it wasn’t a good time to meet me yet, so I went back to Heaven to play with God. We used to watch you. But then you decided you were ready, and I came into your tummy again, and this time I got to meet you. I was so excited. If anyone sees this post and is considering a medical abortion for a terminal diagnosis, I just want to offer you a different perspective. They offered abortion many times. I would be lying if I said that wasn't the worst year of my life (last year). But I knew that as long as he was in there, he was happy, loved, and safe. We made it full term and we got him 9 hrs. It is a certain agony to mourne a still-living child. I was removed. Weepy. My world shrunk to just what was around me. Yet, after it was all said and done, I feel God speak to me, reveal to me, redeem my grief. I am so much wiser by going through the storm, rather than try to go around it, if you will. If anyone needs help with a terminal diagnosis, please reach out. Termination is not your only option unfer most circumstances (not all). Tgere is so much beauty in carrying a terminal baby.
